Abstract
This article explores the use of the humanoid robot Aster in a bilingual special-education classroom to support children diagnosed with autism spectrum condition (ASC). Building on prior human–robot interaction work, the study investigates how guided play sessions with Aster affect communication, social engagement, imitation, and attention during classroom activities. Over an eight-week period, 6 children participated in 96 individual sessions with the robot. Results suggest positive effects in prompted speech, turn-taking, and sustained focus, while teachers reported favorable impressions and proposed additional educational uses for the robot in everyday instruction.

The findings indicate beneficial effects on prompted speech, turn-taking, and sustained attention, and teachers gave positive feedback while suggesting the robot could also be used more broadly in everyday teaching.
